Hey all. We are using the OC as a headless server and ran into a lot of memory issues. We realised that OC reads all the parts/messages in a session before loading it, causing big memory spikes. We recently auto-compacted sessions when users were not using our platform, and after a full wipe of session data, found massive improvements. Hope this helps anyone wanting a quick win while this problem is ongoing.
After update to new version of 1.4.18 the error is gone. Thank you

The same crash fires from the **claude-mem** OpenCode plugin ([thedotmack/claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem)). v12.3.2 (shipped 2026-04-20) still declares `claude_mem_search`'s `args` as a plain JS object (`{query: {type: "string", description: "..."}}`) instead of a Zod schema, so it hits this exact `toJsonSchema(schema._zod.def)` path.

Repro:

1. `npx claude-mem install --ide opencode`
2. launch `opencode`, submit any prompt
3. crash at `#maybeClose` → `#handleOnExit` in `child_process` with `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'n._zod.def')`

Upstream tracks it: [thedotmack/claude-mem#1947](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/1947) is open (reopened by the maintainer after an accidental backlog cleanup), and their [PR #2063](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/pull/2063) tried a fix but closed unmerged.

For now: delete `~/.config/opencode/plugins/claude-mem.js`, or run `opencode --pure`.

None of them change the behavior. Dark/light detection seems completely broken in this version with Ghostty + macOS Tahoe.

I also want this behavior in chat/file-selection workflows.

Selecting text should remain a normal selection first, so users can copy it with standard OS shortcuts (`Cmd/Ctrl+C`) and paste it into the chat input themselves.

`Add to chat` is still useful, but it would be much better as an explicit action (for example a shortcut, toolbar action, or context-menu item) instead of happening immediately on selection.

In short: please prefer `select -> copy -> paste` as the default interaction, and make `select -> add to chat` an explicit opt-in action. That would feel much more natural and predictable.
